LESSON: MANAGEMENT AND CONSERVATION OF THE ENVIRONMENT

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES
Strand: Natural and Historic Built Environments
Topic 4.4: Management and Conservation of the Environment
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 8

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Management and Conservation of the Environment, part of Natural and Historic Built Environments in Grade 9 SOCIAL STUDIES.

Key inquiry question: Why is it important to conserve the degraded environment?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify the selected world heritage sites in Africa,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Management and Conservation of the Environment in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. examine the importance of the selected world sites in promoting cultural heritage,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Management and Conservation of the Environment in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. design measures to conserve the selected world heritage sites,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Management and Conservation of the Environment in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. apply critical thinking skills in conserving heritage sites within the locality.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Management and Conservation of the Environment in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

E. value heritage sites in the community. Learner is guided to: • use digital/print resources to locate the selected world heritage sites • brainstorm on the importance of the selected world sites in promoting cultural heritage, • demonstrate respect for diversity of cultural expression in Kenya as they compose and sing songs or recite poems on the importance of world heritage sites in Africa, • formulate in pairs measures to conserve heritage sites. Why is it important to conserve the world heritage sites?

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Management and Conservation of the Environment in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Management and Conservation of the Environment together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Critical thinking and Problem-solving: learners explore possible solutions and their pro and cons as they develop

communication messages on how to creatively manage and conserve the environment.

• Citizenship: learners demonstrate tolerance, and express and understand different viewpoints as they participate in

environmental conservation in the community.

Values:
• Responsibility: learners engage in assigned roles and duties as they participate in environmental conservation activities in the

community.

• Integrity: learners are committed to duty as they participate in environmental conservation activities in the community.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

• Environmental education: learners participate in environmental conservation in the community.

• Social Cohesion: learners work together in environmental conservation activities in the community.

Link to other Learning Areas:

• Learners use Integrated Science knowledge to research on factors that lead to degradation of the environment in the

community.

• Agriculture is relevant as learners view video clips or documentaries or pictures and write an essay on the factors that leads

degradation of the environment.

5. value heritage sites in the community. Why is it important to conserve the world heritage sites?

Remember the key question: Why is it important to conserve the degraded environment?
